summary: Duncan Town Airport (DCT/MYRD) is a small but vital regional airfield serving Ragged Island, one of the most remote inhabited islands in the southern Bahamas. The airport connects this isolated fishing community to Nassau and other Bahamian hubs, supporting both residents and the island's growing eco-tourism sector. Its modest single-runway configuration reflects the low-volume traffic typical of the Out Islands, yet it remains an essential lifeline for the sparsely populated archipelago.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Duncan Town Airport?
A: Duncan Town is primarily served by Bahamasair and regional charter operators, typically with small turboprop aircraft connecting to Nassau's Lynden Pindling International Airport.

Q: How far is the airport from Duncan Town settlement?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from the small settlement of Duncan Town, with a short taxi or rental vehicle ride typically required.

Q: Is there a terminal building at Duncan Town Airport?
A: The airport has only basic facilities, including a small terminal structure sufficient for the low passenger volumes typical of this remote Out Island destination.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Duncan Town?
A: Flights operate year-round but are most reliable during the dry season from November to April, when weather conditions in the southern Bahamas are most favorable.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options are limited; arrange a rental car or pickup with your accommodation in advance, as taxis are not always readily available at the terminal. Many lodges and guesthouses on Ragged Island offer complimentary airport transfers when booking a stay. Flights are often weather-dependent, so build flexibility into your travel schedule, especially during hurricane season.
local_tip: Pack light and bring all essential supplies, including reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear, and cash, as the island has very limited shopping and no ATMs. Ragged Island is renowned for some of the most pristine bonefishing flats in the Bahamas, so anglers should coordinate with local guides well before arrival.
